info.name: Multistack — Full System (docker-compose.full.yml)
info.description:
Manual/Newman tests for the whole platform brought up by api/tests/manual-test/docker-compose.full.yml.

Services & ports:
  gateway                      http://localhost:8080   (Bearer {{api_key}} — a per-org API key, ADR-026; the `seed-api-key` job seeds sk-e2e-fixed-verify-key-001)
  rate-limiter-rpm             http://localhost:9100    (POST /check)
  rate-limiter-tpm             http://localhost:9110    (POST /check)
  tokenizer                    http://localhost:9300    (POST /tokenize)
  admin-control-plane          http://localhost:9200    (Bearer test-admin-key; local auth at /api/auth/*)
  organization-control-plane   http://localhost:9220    (Bearer test-service-key; local auth at /api/auth/*)

Caps in the full stack (RPM_RATE_LIMITS / TPM_RATE_LIMITS): RPM caps ONLY limited-model=3; TPM caps ONLY tpm-limited-model=15 tokens/min. llama-3-8b / claude are uncapped (no X-RateLimit headers). Counting is ASYNC (ADR-013/AD-01): the limiters count off the NATS backbone (RPM from request events, TPM from response events) and /check only READS — so limits are soft and a burst may overshoot by one; re-send the tripping request if it hasn't flipped yet. Run folders top-to-bottom; the RPM/TPM bursts count against a fixed 60s window (cross a minute boundary and you must re-run the folder).

Local auth (ADR-025, folders 7-9): the docker-compose stack's `seed-admin` one-shot job bootstraps superadmin@platform.local / ChangeMe123! on first `up`. Folders 7-8 rotate it and exercise the full login/refresh/logout/change-password/lockout-adjacent flow for both the org-less Admin CP tier and the org-scoped Org CP tier; folder 9 proves the two services mint one shared JWT contract. Postman's cookie jar carries the HttpOnly refresh cookie automatically between requests to the same host — run each folder top to bottom in one go.

Folders 10-12 cover the modules added after folder 9 was written: the master permission catalog (Admin CP), org-scoped Roles/RBAC + ADR-029 identity-gated user provisioning (Org CP, including the with-owner super-admin flow, default org_admin/org_user role seeding, permission composition, effective-permission resolution, and enforcement via /api/users), and the ADR-026/027/028 per-org API-key lifecycle (mint/list/rotate/update/revoke via the end-user JWT surface, plus the internal verify contract the gateway itself calls — folder 12 step 8 mints a fresh key and immediately spends it against the live gateway to prove the two services agree). Folder 11 depends on folder 7's acp_admin_token (super-admin session) to call the with-owner endpoint; if folder 7 was skipped due to lockout, re-run it first. `admin_key` (test-admin-key) is the super-admin/UI bearer for Admin CP's /v1/* routes; `service_key` (test-service-key) is the inter-service bearer both control planes check on their own /internal/v1/* routes (Org CP's internal calls to Admin CP's permission catalog use this — ADR-029 made that a hard dependency of org creation itself) — the two are DISTINCT secrets, not the same value (council review fix: the super-admin credential no longer doubles as the service credential). `mg_verify_key` (test-mg-verify-key) is a THIRD, even narrower bearer: the model-gateway's own credential for Org CP's GET /internal/v1/api-keys/verify only, distinct from `service_key` so the internet-adjacent gateway can never reach /v1 users/roles/rbac even if compromised.

item.name: 2. RPM burst — limited-model=3 (run in order)
item.description: limited-model is RPM-capped at 3 (its own model counter). Counting is ASYNC (ADR-013): /check reads BEFORE the request is counted, so calls 1-3 allow and the 4th denies once the first 3 have been counted off the NATS queue. Soft limit: if the 4th is still 200, re-send it once.

exec: pm.test.skip('still allowed — consumer catching up (soft limit); re-send this request');

item.name: 3. TPM burst — tpm-limited-model=15 tokens (run in order)
item.description: tpm-limited-model is TPM-capped at 15 tokens/min. The mock returns usage.total_tokens=9 per chat call, and TPM counts async from RESPONSE events (AD-01/AD-02). So call 1 (counter 0) and call 2 (counter 9) allow; by call 3 the counter is 18 (>=15) and it denies. Soft/async: if call 3 is still 200, the response consumer hasn't drained yet — re-send it once.

exec: pm.test('200 allow (counter still < 15 at read time)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test.skip('still allowed — TPM response-event consumer catching up (soft limit); re-send this request');

item.name: 4. Policy /check direct (READ-ONLY)
item.description: Call the policy services directly (the same contract the gateway uses). /check NEVER counts (ADR-013/AD-01) — counting is only via the NATS consumers off gateway events — so hammering /check here never denies; it just reads current counters.

exec: // decision depends on how full the 60s window is (folder 2 may have filled it) — assert the contract, not a fixed decision.
pm.test('bare allow (no budget fields)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.eql({ decision: 'allow' }));
// decision depends on the 60s window state (folder 3 may have filled it) — assert the contract.

item.name: 6. Admin Control Plane (:9200)
item.description: Plans + Organizations CRUD behind a fixed super-admin bearer (test-admin-key). Run in order — it creates a plan + org, exercises the 422/409 rules, then cleans up so the folder is re-runnable. Chained ids are stored in collection variables acp_plan_id / acp_org_id.

exec: pm.test('Free is_default true, tpm 10000', () => { pm.expect(free.is_default).to.be.true; pm.expect(free.tpm).to.eql(10000); });

item.name: orgs: create with valid plan -> 201 (save acp_org_id)
7. Local Auth — Admin Control Plane (ADR-025)
item.description: Org-less super-admin local auth. The compose stack's `seed-admin` one-shot job already bootstrapped {{seed_admin_email}} / {{seed_admin_password}} with must_change_password=true. This folder rotates it, exercises the forced-rotation gate, no-account-enumeration, refresh rotation, and logout. Run top to bottom — each step depends on the collection variable the previous step set. Re-running the whole collection after a fresh `docker compose down -v && up` resets the seed password back to {{seed_admin_password}}.

exec: pm.test('no org on the response', () => pm.expect(j.org).to.be.undefined);
// Locked out from repeated prior wrong-password attempts against this fixed seed email
// (can't be made unique per run, unlike alice's). Try the fallback anyway — harmless if
// it also 429s, its own script handles that gracefully.
pm.test.skip('seed admin currently locked out (429) — trying the fallback login');
// The seed password only works once — a prior run against this same (not-torn-down)
// stack already rotated it. Jump to the fallback login instead of failing the run.
pm.test('seed password rejected (401) — already rotated by an earlier run', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(401));

item.name: login: fallback (already-rotated admin)
item.description: Only reached when the seed password above was rejected — i.e. this stack already had folder 7 run against it before. Logs in with the fixed password that 'password: rotate seed password' always rotates to, then jumps straight past the rotation-demo steps (already done in a prior run) to the shared tail.

exec: // Genuinely locked out (enough real wrong-password attempts accumulated across
// several rapid collection runs). No admin token is obtainable right now, so skip
// the rest of folder 7 AND folder 9 (which needs this token) rather than cascade into
// false failures — folder 8 (org auth) is fully independent and still runs in full.
// Wait out the backoff window (or restart the stack) to exercise folder 7/9 again.
pm.test.skip('admin still locked out (429) — skipping the rest of folder 7 and folder 9');
postman.setNextRequest('plans: get Free id (for org creation)');
pm.test('200 (already-rotated password from a prior run)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: password: too weak -> 422 (rotation gate still lets this through)
admin: no enumeration: unknown email -> 401 invalid_credentials
admin: no enumeration: wrong password -> byte-identical 401 body

exec: // The seed admin's email is fixed forever (can't be made unique per run like alice's),
// so repeated back-to-back COLLECTION runs can genuinely trip its lockout counter
// (LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS) after enough wrong-password attempts accumulate in Redis. A
// 429 here means the brute-force defense is working correctly, not that no-enumeration
// broke — it just means the account is currently rate-limited. Wait out
// LOGIN_BACKOFF_*_SECONDS (or restart the stack) to see the plain 401 path again.
pm.test.skip('seed admin temporarily locked out from repeated prior runs (429) — no-enumeration still holds, just gated earlier');
pm.test('identical body to the unknown-email case (no enumeration)', () => pm.expect(JSON.stringify(j)).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('acp_unknown_email_body')));

item.name: admin: refresh rotates the access token
8. Local Auth — Organization Control Plane (ADR-025)
item.description: Org-scoped user local auth on top of the existing users/organizations model. Creates a fresh org via Admin CP (which provisions it into Org CP synchronously, ADR-018), then an org user WITH an initial password (the admin-initiated provisioning path — there is no public self-register). Run top to bottom.

item.name: plans: get Free id (for org creation)
orgs: create AuthTestOrg -> 201 (provisions into Org CP too)

exec: pm.test('status active (Org CP provisioning succeeded)', () => pm.expect(j.status).to.eql('active'));
// Org CP's local-auth login looks up users by email GLOBALLY (no org scoping in the
// lookup query), but email is only unique PER ORG — so a leftover 'alice@...' row in an
// old, uncleaned-up org from a previous run would collide. Make the email unique per run.

item.name: org-cp: create user with a weak password -> 422 weak_password
login: alice (must_change_password=true, forced by admin provisioning)
no enumeration: wrong password -> byte-identical 401 body

exec: pm.test('identical body to the unknown-email case (no enumeration)', () => pm.expect(JSON.stringify(j)).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('org_unknown_email_body')));

item.name: org-cp: admin resets alice's password -> 200 (forces rotation again)
login: admin-reset password works, must_change_password=true again
orgs: delete AuthTestOrg -> 204 (cleanup, matches folder 6's hygiene)
item.description: Deletes via Admin CP (which owns organizations). Belt-and-braces alongside the per-run-unique org name/email: keeps the DB from accumulating a fresh org on every run.

item.name: 9. Cross-Service JWT Contract (ADR-025)
item.description: Proves live what api/tests/contract/test_jwt_contract.py pins offline: Admin CP and Org CP mint the SAME HS256 claim shape under the shared JWT_SECRET, differing only in the `org` claim. Requires folders 7 and 8 to have run first (uses their last-issued tokens). Piggybacks the assertion onto a harmless GET so no new endpoint is needed — this step never touches gateway state.

item.name: assert shared claim shape (decode both tokens client-side)

exec: pm.test('admin token has the required claims', () => required.forEach(k => pm.expect(adminClaims).to.have.property(k)));
pm.test('org token has the required claims', () => required.forEach(k => pm.expect(orgClaims).to.have.property(k)));
pm.test('admin token has NO org claim', () => pm.expect(adminClaims.org).to.be.undefined);
pm.test('org token HAS an org claim', () => pm.expect(orgClaims.org).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('auth_org_id')));
pm.test('claim-key sets match except for org (no drift between the two encoders)', () => pm.expect(orgKeysSansOrg).to.eql(adminKeysSansOrg));

item.name: 10. Permissions Catalog (Admin CP master list)
item.description: The master permission list Admin CP owns (ADR-019) — Org CP only ever validates permission ids against it, never writes it. Self-contained: creates and cleans up its own throwaway permission. Also proves the ADMIN_API_KEY/SERVICE_API_KEY fix (see docker-compose.full.yml) by hitting Org CP's live read-through proxy at the end.

exec: pm.test('has the full default catalog', () => expected.forEach(s => pm.expect(slugs).to.include(s)));

item.name: permissions: internal list -> 200 includes custom (Org CP's validation seam)
org-cp: permissions proxy -> 200 (same catalog, proves the shared key config)

exec: pm.test('200 (Org CP -> Admin CP internal call authenticated)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('includes widgets.manage (live proxy, not a stale copy)', () => pm.expect(slugs).to.include('widgets.manage'));

item.name: 11. Roles & RBAC + Identity-Gated Provisioning (Org CP, ADR-029)
item.description: Org-scoped role CRUD, permission composition, user-role assignment, and effective-permission resolution — plus the identity-gated /api/users surface (the first route to enforce require_permission). Self-contained: creates its own org (proving seed_default_roles' org_admin/org_user auto-seeding), an owner, and a member. Does NOT clean up its org — folder 12 (API Keys) reuses it and deletes it at the very end. Run 11 then 12 together.

item.name: plans: get Free id (for RBAC org)
orgs: create RbacOrg -> 201 (default org_admin/org_user roles auto-seeded)

exec: pm.test('201 (seed_default_roles succeeded — proves the shared admin/service key fix)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));

item.name: roles: list seeded default roles -> org_admin + org_user present
roles: org_admin has all 13 default permissions
org-cp: create owner user WITH password -> 201
roles: assign org_admin role to owner -> 200
permissions: get users.update id (for auditor role)

exec: pm.test('users.update exists in the catalog', () => pm.expect(perm).to.not.be.undefined);

item.name: roles: set permissions with unknown id -> 422

exec: pm.test('422 (Admin CP catalog validation, fail-closed before any write)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(422));

item.name: api-users: owner (org_admin, has users.create) creates a member via /api/users -> 201

exec: pm.test('201 (identity-gated: org taken from the caller\'s own token, ADR-029)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));

item.name: roles: new member auto-assigned org_user default role
rbac: effective permissions for member -> org_user defaults (3)
roles: compose member roles -> org_user + auditor
rbac: effective permissions for member -> union now 4 (adds users.update)

exec: pm.test('union across roles: 4 distinct ids', () => pm.expect(ids).to.have.lengthOf(4));

item.name: rbac: internal composed roles view for member -> 2 roles with permission_ids

exec: pm.test('403 (require_permission fails closed on a missing grant)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

item.name: rbac: effective permissions for member reverts to 3 (auditor's grant is gone)
12. API Keys (Org CP, ADR-026/027/028) — mint, rotate, revoke, spend on the gateway
item.description: The end-user JWT surface for per-org API keys, gated by the granular apikey.create/update/delete permissions (org_admin has them, org_user doesn't). Reuses folder 11's org/owner/member — run 11 then 12. Ends by deleting the shared org (cleanup for both folders). Steps 8/10/11/14 round-trip a freshly minted key against the LIVE gateway (:8080) to prove the mint -> hash -> Org CP verify -> Redis cache chain end to end.

item.name: api-keys: owner creates a key with a future expiry -> 201 (raw_key once)

exec: pm.test('prefix is a safe display fragment', () => pm.expect(j.prefix.startsWith('sk-')).to.be.true);
pm.test('raw_key present (only time it ever is)', () => pm.expect(j.raw_key).to.be.a('string'));
pm.test('no raw_key on any entry', () => keys.forEach(k => pm.expect(k.raw_key).to.be.undefined));

item.name: gateway: the minted key authenticates -> 200 (org-cp verify + Redis cache)

exec: pm.test('200 (rotate has no explicit status_code, defaults to FastAPI\'s 200)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: gateway: OLD raw key rejected after rotation -> 401 (cache evicted)
api-keys: internal verify by hash (gateway's own contract, mg verify key)
